source: d3-celestial data/mw.json, d3-celestial commit 7e720a3de062059d4c5400a379146a601d9010e0 (master, 2022-07-05) (from J. R. Vieira's Milky Way Outline Catalog)
format: levels[]: level 1 = faintest/outermost outline .. 5 = brightest; d3-celestial draws each level as its own translucent layer on top of the previous ones. polygons: closed rings of [raDeg 0..360, decDeg] (J2000), consecutive points < 2 deg apart, edges taken along the shorter RA direction. Two level-1 rings wrap once around the sky in RA (the band's northern and southern edges); the other rings are small outlines or holes. Membership rule for every level: cast a ray from the point due north along its meridian to the pole and count crossings with all of that level's rings (edges interpolated linearly in RA/Dec); odd = inside. On screen this is an even-odd fill, provided the two wrap-around rings are clipped/closed consistently.
